Aggrieved by the impugned order dated 23.9.2024, the Review Petitioner has made - f) The Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana granted a stay on the order dated 25.10.2021 vide its interim order dated 1.6.2022 in CM-1005-LPA-2022 in LPA1115-2021 and CM-1006-LPA-2022 in LPA-1116-2021, and non-consideration of the same in the impugned order is an error apparent on record. - g) The Review Petitioner was unable to take any action due to the operation of the interim order dated 1.6.2022 until the disposal of LPA Nos. 1115, 1116, and 1121 of 2021 by the Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana on 16.12.2022. Immediately after the final order was passed on 16.12.2022, the Review Petitioner, vide letter dated 19.12.2022, informed the Deputy Commissioner of SAS Nagar, Mohali, that since the LPAs had been dismissed, the Review Petitioner was ready to complete the work within a week. The Review Petitioner had arranged all necessary manpower, materials, and tools. The Review Petitioner also requested appropriate protection to ensure that the work could be completed smoothly without any law and order issues. The letter dated 19.12.2022 clearly showed that the Review Petitioner was, in fact, prepared to complete its work within the time, but was prevented from doing so due to the interim order dated 1.6.2022 of the Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana in the aforementioned LPAs. 5. The matter was admitted on 14.1.2025, and notice was issued to the Respondents. However, none of the Respondents has filed their reply in the matter. After hearing the Review Petitioner, the order in the matter was reserved on 20.3.2025. 6. The instant Review Petition has been filed under Section 94(1) of the Act read with Section 114 and Order 47 Rule 1 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 and Regulation 52 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 (“CBR, 2023”) seeking review of the order dated 23.9.2024 passed by the Commission in Petition No. 328/TT/2023. Under Section 94(1)(f) of the Act, the Commission is vested with the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in the matter of “reviewing its decision, directions and orders”. Regulation 52(2) of the CBR, 2023 provides the following grounds on which an aggrieved person can seek the review of a direction, decision or order of the Commission, which are akin to the grounds provided in Order 47 Rule 1 of CPC: (2) Any person aggrieved by a direction, decision, or order of the Commission, from which no appeal has been preferred, may file a review petition on the following grounds within forty days of the making of such decision, direction, or order: 7. In the present case, the Review Petitioner has sought the review of the impugned order on the grounds of error apparent on the face of the record and other sufficient reasons, which are dealt with in the subsequent paragraphs. 9. We have given our thoughtful consideration to the contentions of the Review Petitioner and have perused the record, including the impugned order. 10. The case of the Review Petitioner is that the impugned order, in particular, the observation of the Commission in paragraph 59 of the impugned order, is erroneous. Before we examine the contentions of the Review Petitioner, we think it appropriate to refer to the following relevant excerpts of the impugned order: 15. In paragraph 53 of the impugned order, the facts concerning the orders dated 22.10.2020 and 9.11.2020 of the District Magistrate being challenged before the Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana in CWP Nos.19391 of 2020 and 5181 of 2021 on 4.3.2021, are recorded. This paragraph also discusses the District Magistrate’s said orders being affirmed by the Hon’ble High Court vide judgment dated 25.10.2021 in the said CWPs, with the observation that the Petitioner shall not lay the transmission line before the relocation of the temporary huts of the labourers. This paragraph further speaks about a Committee formed 21. As regards the contention of the Review Petitioner that in the LPA Nos. 1115, 1116 and 1121, which were filed by the landowners challenging the order dated 25.10.2021, an interim order was passed on 1.6.2022. The non-consideration of the same in the impugned order is an error apparent on record. To deal with this contention of the Review Petitioner, we think it necessary to reproduce the snapshot of the order dated 1.6.2022 in CM-1005LPA-2022 in LPA-1115-2021 and CM-1006-LPA-2022 in LPA-1116-2021, which is as follows: 22. It is noticed that above order dated 1.6.2022 in CM-1005-LPA-2022 in LPA-1115-2021 and CM-1006-LPA-2022 in LPA-1116-2021, clearly recorded the submissions of the learned senior counsel for Respondent No.4 made during the course of the hearing before the Hon’ble High Court that the process of installation of one transmission tower falling within the territory owned by the appellant was not being so constructed and would also not be processed till the next date of hearing till relocation. Therefore, we are of the view that the said order of the Hon’ble High Court, in any way, cannot be said to be a direction, and these are mere submissions of the learned senior counsel for Respondent No. 4 23. For the reasons mentioned above in detail, we find no substance in the contentions of the Review Petitioner. Therefore, the Review Petitioner's contentions are rejected.
